highlights.title: Approve AI meal requests on iPhone and Apple Watch
changes: AI assistants can request meal logging and open Trio's iPhone Treatments or Watch Confirm screen.
A new "Allow meal requests" switch is off by default.

The automated setup will still add Push Notifications for the watch app.

includedPullRequests.title: feat(ai-requests): Finish an assistant's meal request in Trio's own Treatments sheet and watch Confirm screen
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

An AI assistant asks trio-rc to log a meal. trio-rc wakes Trio, which works out its suggested dose and asks the wearer. The wearer finishes the request in **Trio's own screens**:
- on the iPhone, the **Treatments** sheet, filled in;
- on the watch, the bolus **Confirm** screen.

The wearer confirms the normal way, and Trio reports what was actually logged and given. **"Allow meal requests" is off by default.**

Since the first draft, the custom approval screens and signed answers have been replaced by the existing screens (decisions D1–D17 in `notes/plans/2026-10-21-meal-requests-existing-screens-decisions.md`).

```text
request arrives (trio-rc)
  AIRequestCoordinator.receive        # dose for the notification text; pending; watch first, iPhone after the delay
  iPhone: tap / bring Trio to front   # opens Treatments filled in (carbs, fat/protein if entries are on, "AI: ChatGPT – pizza slice")
    upstream "Log Carbs and Enact Bolus" (its own checks, warnings, Face ID)
    AIRequestTreatmentsSession        # claims the request; outcome from this bolus's own pump event
  watch: Review                       # asks the phone for live amounts, opens straight on Confirm (Back to adjust)
    upstream crown confirm / Log Carbs → one confirm over WatchConnectivity → the phone logs and boluses
  whichever device goes first takes it, through one lock; the other closes its screen ("Logged on your watch")
  report to trio-rc                   # delivering / logged / declined / expired: what was actually done
```

**Upstream footprint:** only one-line hooks.

| Where | Hook |
|---|---|
| Treatments sheet | 2 lines: the decimal formatter for a request's grams, and the session modifier |
| Treatments state model | 1 line: `refusesSubmit` |
| `TrioApp` | 2 renamed lines |
| Watch main view | 1 line |
| `WatchState+Requests` | 2 lines: the intercepts |
| Confirm screen's carbs row | 1 line |

Plus the existing one-line hooks. Upstream's algorithm, `APSManager`, `CarbsStorage` and `BolusSafetyValidator` are untouched, and manual Treatments and watch entries behave as before.

**Removed:**
- the custom iPhone and watch approval screens;
- test requests;
- signed answers and the display MAC;
- the "Approve from the notification" style;
- answer routes;
- the AI-only checks (D1).

The notification keeps the dose line, fat and protein (when logged) and the 0 U reason.

**Since review** (`130e2501e`, `5858b52e3`, `42fe9c046`, `b2e3998bf`):
- A manual watch entry started over a request's screens declines the request and starts from zero, as upstream's does. The request's carbs and dose aren't left underneath it.
- A request with only fat or protein is refused when it arrives while fat and protein entries are off: Trio would log nothing for it. The assistant hears "Not given: Fat and protein entries are off in Trio."
- The AI food chat doesn't stop the Treatments sheet closing itself after Log: checked on iOS 26.5 and 27. The comments that said it did are corrected.
- The watch hears how its confirm went as soon as the pump accepts the bolus, as upstream's watch does. It no longer waits for Trio's post-bolus loop update and the report to trio-rc, which could take up to about 2 minutes on a bad network.
- Only one device can carry out a request. The iPhone's Log takes the request through a lock before upstream's submit starts, and the watch's confirm takes it through the same lock, so the two can't both log and bolus for one meal. A watch confirm that loses is told "Logged on your iPhone".
- Trio's request files are read again until they can be. Before the first unlock they're there but can't be read. Trio used to take the seen IDs and final reports as empty and delete the pending request, so after a restart a request it had already handled could be asked again. A request that arrives meanwhile is now left for the next check-in.
- Clearing the watch's notification no longer declines a request that's open on the iPhone's Treatments sheet: the sheet answers it. Leaving the watch's Confirm screens still declines (D11). The settings footer says so.
- The watch asks to show notifications only once meal requests are on, and only then does the phone send trio-rc the watch's push token. Before, every user of this build got the watch's prompt, with the switch on or off.

**Deploy order (changed): deploy trio-rc first** (gordolio/trio-rc#2), then this build. This build's pending report leaves out `approvalStyle` and `answerRoute`, which today's trio-rc requires.

## Evidence

**Tests:** the full suite passes on `b2e3998bf` (1,499 Swift Testing + 3 XCTest), and the watch builds. Each fix since review has tests that were checked to fail with the fix taken out. Each of the 7 tasks was reviewed. The dosing tasks took two fix rounds each. A final whole-branch review and its fix wave are clean.

### iPhone

| Settings | Request opens Treatments | Logged on the watch |
|---|---|---|
| ![AI Assistants settings: Allow meal requests and Ask on iPhone, no style picker, no test requests](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a08cad82-b8ef-4df6-ad26-a8d85fec6e37) | ![Treatments sheet filled in: 82.5 g carbs, note AI: ChatGPT – pizza slice, Bolus 0 until the recommendation is tapped](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ca6347c-6636-4004-a730-cfd1261e37f2) | ![The sheet closed with the banner Logged on your watch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18c4c1b0-51e2-4fa0-bacc-2e0f5323b8a1) |

The settings screenshot predates the footer's new wording ("…declines it, unless it's open on your iPhone").

Request notification → Treatments filled in → Log Carbs:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b81b0d1-7e76-40dc-b6e3-61a24df32307

The iPhone sheet closes when the watch logs the request (D16):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/160f819a-4297-44af-84d4-6c2539ae560c

### Apple Watch

| Notification | Review opens Confirm | Back: bolus screen | Back again: carbs, "Proceed" | Logged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ![Doorbell notification with Review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46eb4c98-1365-48e3-8cd0-f18d3fdb8ac5) | ![Upstream Confirm screen: Carbs 82.5 g, Bolus 0.00 U, dial crown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecc820f6-daed-419f-9af7-b099704db884) | ![Upstream bolus screen: 83 g, 0.00 U, No Bolus, Log Carbs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61d265ee-f589-4e98-8b3b-1e61bfcb423b) | ![Upstream carbs screen showing Proceed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af3fbd3c-2749-43b9-b4a4-748e5773f0ea) | ![Carbs logged successfully](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75b405b8-99b5-4d77-a867-9e6d97a54e5b) |

Notification → Review → Confirm → Back → "No Bolus, Log Carbs" → upstream's acknowledgement:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d415e50-2b33-486e-a7ab-453912e6e71b

Trio's database after these runs shows:
- the watch path logged the request's exact 82.5 g, with the note "AI: ChatGPT – pizza slice";
- the iPhone path logged the same;
- upstream's own watch Meal entry logged "10 g, Via Watch", unchanged.

**Simulator limits:**
- **Where the requests came from.** This build has no trio-rc host, so requests were written into Trio's pending file, and the watch's doorbell was sent with `simctl push` in trio-rc's new shape.
- **Dose and confirm.** Trio's dose is 0 U (no pump or loop), and the crown can't be turned in the simulator. So the watch path was confirmed with "No Bolus, Log Carbs", which goes through the same intercept as the crown.
- **Not checked here:** a real bolus, Face ID with a pump, the 41 mm layout, and the watch's notification prompt appearing once meal requests are turned on (built, not run).

**Found while testing, a decision for you:**
- On a branch build, Trio shows the "Hey Trioneer, watch out!" alert at every launch.
- A cold-launch tap of the iPhone request notification therefore finds that alert up. By D15 (no queue, nothing opens over another sheet), the sheet doesn't open. Trio logs "another sheet is open, so … isn't opened".
- Release builds don't show the alert. With Trio already running, the tap opens the sheet.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Fork code sits behind a switch that's off by default, and the hooks are one line each. There are no Core Data model changes. Saved files and preferences from the previous build still load.

**Blast Radius:** dosing.

With the switch on, a request fills in the screens the wearer already uses. Nothing is logged or given until the wearer confirms there, and upstream's own checks and Face ID apply.

**Follow-ups, recorded and not done here:**
- **Working without the phone:** approving on the watch when the phone is out of reach. Signing made this possible, and it's to be refined (spec "Later").
- **The prefilled note:** when it's longer than 25 characters it can only be replaced, not edited character by character (upstream's text field limit).
- **Clock skew:** trio-rc's 660 s grace leaves 60 s of skew against Trio's 600 s hold.
- **Back to the watch's carbs screen:** it shows 0 g with Proceed off, because upstream's carbs screen doesn't read the request's carbs. The wearer dials them again, and a value other than the request's rounded grams is logged as the watch's whole grams.
- **Smaller ones**, under "Deferred minors (Trio)" in `notes/reviews/2026-10-21-meal-requests-rulings.md`:
  - the watch keeps a request's notification after logging it there;
  - upstream's notification categories can overwrite the watch's on a first launch;
  - cleanups: the unused wake-up push type, a duplicated key, and the full status snapshot built for the 0 U reason.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * AI assistants can request meal logging and insulin approval through the iPhone or Apple Watch. Review the request, edit meal details, and approve or decline before anything is logged or delivered.
  * Configure whether to allow meal requests and how long to wait before asking on iPhone if there’s no watch response.
  * Requests show their details, expiration, and outcome; notifications can open the relevant approval screen.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of request delivery, duplicate requests, interruptions, and sign-in changes.
